complexity.notes: Naming the local variable `dict` shadows the built-in type. A simpler idiom is a single pass with a set, returning True on the first element already seen; alternatively `len(nums) != len(set(nums))`. Since values are bounded by 4n+1, hashing could also be avoided with a fixed-size boolean array or a bitset for guaranteed O(n) worst case.
complexity.summary: Counts occurrences of each value in a dict over the array, then makes a second pass to check whether any count exceeds 1. Correct but does two passes where one would suffice.
